proposals.evidence: DEDR1041 explicitly gives Tamil ōṭu, Malayalam ōṭuka, Kannada ōḍu and Kodagu ōḍ- to run. Survey Irula oḍu/oḍɨ and Alu Kurumba voḍu preserve the southern run stem, including initial glide and source inflection. The article’s explicit Telugu loan in Gondi and questioned Kui comparison are not used. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4004 gives Tamil/Malayalam paḻam ripe fruit, Irula pammu/pāmu, Toda pum, Kannada paṇṇu, Parji pal, Gondi paṇḍ(i) and Konda paṇḍu. Selected survey paḷam/payam/pagam/paśam/pām- responses preserve lect-specific reflexes or loss of the medial retroflex, and Kannada/related annu reflects loss of initial h-. These are comparative family proposals; the separate Indo-Aryan-looking phal forms and opaque responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR4753 gives Tamil maḻai, Malayalam maḻa, Kannada maḻe, Kodagu/Tulu maḷe, Kota may and Toda maw rain. These selected southern survey forms preserve lect-specific lateral, glide, velar or sibilant reflexes and contractions of the rain stem. Minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions; ambiguous source fragments and Indo-Aryan-looking varṣa forms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
